summary: Asks IANA to create a registry for PIM message types, lists initial contents from existing RFCs and sets a registration procedure. It also reserves one type for future extension. It is a proposed standard and was replaced by RFC 8736.

eli5.summary: An official list of message labels used by multicast routers, with rules for adding new ones.

subtitle: A central registry for Protocol Independent Multicast message types.

tldr.problem: PIM version 2 lacked an IANA registry for message types, even though multiple RFCs were defining them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6166 creates a registry, populates it with existing message types from RFCs 3973, 4601, and 5015, sets an IETF Review policy for new types, and reserves one type for future extension.
tldr.outcome: PIM message types are now centrally documented and managed through a standardized process.

today: RFC 6166 is a Proposed Standard that was obsoleted by RFC 8736. The PIM message type registry continues to be maintained by IANA.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM) is used by routers to manage multicast groups. PIM version 1 used the IGMP protocol and had a registry for message types, but PIM version 2 is independent and needed its own registry. Multiple RFCs like RFC 3973 (PIM Dense Mode), RFC 4601 (PIM Sparse Mode), and RFC 5015 (Bidirectional PIM) defined new message types without a central place to list them all.
sections.eli5: Multicast routers need to understand different kinds of messages. Different RFCs added new message types, so they needed a checklist.

sections.title: The Registry
sections.content: RFC 6166 creates a PIM message type registry in the Protocol Independent Multicast branch at IANA. The message type field is 4 bits, allowing values from 0 to 15. The initial registry includes 10 assigned types: Hello, Register, Register Stop, Join/Prune, Bootstrap, Assert, Graft, Graft-Ack, Candidate RP Advertisement, and State Refresh. Types 11-14 are unassigned, and type 15 is reserved for future extension of the message type space. New types are assigned through IETF Review, meaning they must be defined in a published RFC.
sections.eli5: There are 16 numbered slots (0-15) for different message types. Ten are already taken, four are open, and one is saved for if they need to expand in the future.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 6166 is a Proposed Standard that was obsoleted by RFC 8736. The PIM message type registry it created is maintained by IANA.
sections.eli5: This RFC set up the message type list. A newer RFC (8736) has since taken over the role.
